FINDINGS:

The response is heavy because GET /api/orchestrators returns full session records. In app/routes/system.py:list_orchestrators, active orchestrators are serialized with AgentSession.to_dict() from app/session.py. That includes system_prompt (up to 500 characters), description, owned_dirs, task and token counters, and other session metadata. Database-only orchestrators come from get_all_sessions() and include all stored columns. The route then adds last_turn_ts, any_running, any_waiting, and cache-policy fields. The code identifies a separate list endpoint’s large fields—system_prompt and last_summary—as omitted there because consumers do not read them (app/manager.py:_LIST_OMIT), but that omission is not applied to this route.

Consumers found:

- Dashboard app.js:loadOrchestrators reads parent_name for filtering, and uses name, scope, id, status, cost_usd, context_pct, model, color, cache_ttl_seconds, cache_ttl_approximate, and last_turn_ts for tabs, selection, and cache pills. Tab status also uses any_running and any_waiting. Its 60-second refresh updates unread indicators from status and scope.
- Dashboard app.js:refreshSessions uses the same route to update unread indicators; it reads name, status, and scope.
- app/mcp_stdio.py:list_orchestrators formats name, scope, status, cost_usd, context_pct, and description.
- app/routes/system.py itself derives any_running and any_waiting from scope and live session state.

No located consumer of GET /api/orchestrators reads system_prompt, owned_dirs, task_id, token/tool counters, or most other session metadata. The MCP listing does read description, so dropping that field would change its output.

The cut belongs in app/routes/system.py:list_orchestrators: construct a dedicated, compact orchestrator listing with the fields above instead of returning full `to_dict()`/database rows. Preserve description for MCP, and preserve the dashboard fields, including cache metadata and parent_name. This should reduce payload without breaking the identified consumers; confirm against any external clients before treating the field list as a universal API contract.

The startup duplicate has two independent callers: DOMContentLoaded calls loadOrchestrators(), and the first scheduled refresh calls refreshSessions(), which requests /api/orchestrators when its 15-second freshness window is empty. The refresh timer starts at 3 seconds, so both initial requests can overlap. The endpoint is also refreshed every 60 seconds by _startCacheCountdown(). Recommendation: return a compact, explicitly shaped response and avoid the initial duplicate by sharing the startup result with refreshSessions or deferring its orchestrator poll until the freshness interval expires.
